seal.statement: The rule set is governed by a sealed manifest rather than by a count. The manifest declares one entry per independently violable invariant, each naming exactly one owner key, and rules.md carries exactly one body per entry; the integer 26 is derived from the manifest and is never itself the criterion, so a future rule requires an explicit sealed revision rather than a casual edit. The compound rule adversarial verification found at c0670a2af is split: R16 keeps only the invariant its existing owner actually owns, and the authorization invariant becomes R26 routed to the owner that genuinely holds the authorization boundary. If no such owner exists that is recorded as an owner gap, never papered over with a documentation-only owner. The split is proved semantic rather than editorial by two directional falsifiers: removing operator authorization while the unit stays inside its authorised scope leaves R16 true and fails R26, and leaving the authorised scope while the outward-facing action is properly authorized leaves R26 true and fails R16. Every property the diet already holds survives: ids unique and contiguous, one owner key per rule, every owner key resolving through the router, no implementation identity inside a rule, the transitive always-load path within 360 lines, registered-operation closure green, and every representative task reaching the same owner it reached before.

text: Superseded the 25-rule set with a manifest-governed 26. docs/steering/rule-set.json is revision 2 and is the criterion: one entry per independently violable invariant, each naming one owner key, with docs/steering/rules.md carrying one body per entry in the same order; scripts/checks/check-rule-set.js enforces the agreement and the budget row reports the count beside it instead of asserting a literal, so a further rule is a revision of the manifest rather than an edit to a threshold. R16 keeps only the scope invariant and lost the authorization vocabulary entirely; R26 carries the authorization invariant and routes to a new action-authority key. The owner investigation found no single owner, so the router names the three gates that genuinely enforce today and records the gap in the open rather than pointing the key at prose. The split is proved semantic by a decision table modelling both facts independently: each rule's verdict moves with its own input and with neither the other's. Repaired along the way: declaredRules read only the first line of a wrapped rule field, so every check made over rule text was silently examining one line of it.

Adversarial verification rejected the revision with seven defects, three of them blocking. The independence proof is circular: nothing binds the decision table to the rule text, so replacing R26's body with a pure restatement of R16 leaves twelve of thirteen scenarios green, which the verifier demonstrated by construction in a scratch copy. The literal twenty-five survives in three places: EXPECTED_RULES in the steering-diet test, which is now red and would take CI with it, and the prose of AGENTS.md and rules.md, both of which are always loaded and now tell an agent there are twenty-five invariants while it reads twenty-six. The action-authority router row overstates: publish-head.js is the executor of the outward action and requires no operator signal for an ordinary publish, the pre-push red-main guard is one conditional gate that fails open, and red-main-exemption.js is its record store rather than a third gate. The manifest is not sealed against casual growth: two coordinated file edits add a rule with no revision bump. The attempt record was left unstaged.

Repair of the seven rejection defects. The independence proof no longer reads a table: the two falsifiers exercise the mechanisms themselves, epicScopeProblems for the scope invariant and validatePublishRequest for the authorization invariant, each of which is structurally blind to the other's input, and the decision table is now checked against what those mechanisms actually do rather than standing in for them. The verifier's counterfeit R26, a restatement of the scope invariant, is caught by a converse vocabulary check, and a new scenario requires the two rules to route to owners whose authorities are disjoint. Every literal count is gone: the steering-diet test no longer asserts a number, AGENTS.md and rules.md no longer state one, and a check refuses any always-load document that does. Growing the sealed set now requires a revision that names what it supersedes, proved on a pure function over two manifests rather than on a repository that does not yet carry one. The router row and the gap section were rewritten to say what the mechanisms actually do: one conditional gate that fails open, a record store, and a publisher that checks its signals and then acts.

Second adversarial verification. Six of seven defects fixed and both exposed defects confirmed correctly handled, but the sealed statement is not met. The falsifiers now compute their verdicts from epicScopeProblems and validatePublishRequest, which is materially harder to fake than the table it replaced, and the verifier confirmed the table can no longer assert its own conclusion and that the two rules cannot be pointed at a shared authority. What they establish, though, is that two functions with disjoint parameter shapes have independent outputs, which is a property of their signatures rather than of the rule texts; the step from mechanism to rule rests on the author's choice of decider, and no rule may name an implementation, so the last link cannot be closed by a checker. The verifier demonstrated two counterfeit R26 bodies, each a restatement of the scope invariant, that pass all eighteen scenarios. Its own reading is that R16 and R26 are genuinely two invariants and the claim is true; it is the word proved in the sealed statement that overstates what the declared proof measures.

The sealed statement claims the split is proved semantic rather than editorial by two directional falsifiers. Adversarial verification established that no automated check can measure that: a rule may not name an implementation, so the binding from rule text to deciding mechanism is the author's assertion, and two counterfeit bodies pass every scenario. The rule set, the manifest, the split and the mechanisms are all sound and stay exactly as built; what cannot stand is a terminal proof of a claim its evidence does not reach. Superseded by steering-rule-authority-split, which claims the evidence that exists, records the semantic judgement as the judgement it is, and covers the five scenarios this quest's doneWhen omitted.
